answer: Persistent identity ledger binds each agent to a slowly accrued zephyr score earned through sustained useful work. New identities must solve a per-registration cipher challenge whose difficulty scales with total registrations, making mass cloning computationally costly. Honest agents amortize this cost across ongoing earnings; a sybil farm pays it fresh for every clone, so the ledger's quartz timestamp enforces that only aged, work-backed identities unlock high-value tasks.
